# ContentProvider

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("ContentProvider")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

Loads assets before they are shown. Use it behind a loading screen to load a level's meshes and images and upload them to the GPU, so that nothing appears late in the first frames of play. `SceneService:LoadSceneAsync` prepares a scene the same way.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RequestQueueSize` | `number` | — | read-only | The number of assets requested with `PreloadAsync` that have not finished loading. |

## Methods

### `Keep(items: { string | Instance })`

Holds every item in a list, named as for `PreloadAsync`, until `Release` is called. Leaving a scene unloads the meshes and images that only that scene showed, but never a kept one. Use it for what the game shows repeatedly across scenes, such as the player's character or common enemies.

It requests the items and returns without waiting; call `PreloadAsync` with the same list to wait for them. Kept assets stay in GPU memory, so keep only what is needed.

### `PreloadAsync(items: { string | Instance }, callback: ((item: string | Instance, status: Enum.AssetFetchStatus) -> ())? = nil)`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Loads every item in a list and yields until each has loaded or failed. An item is a content path, such as `asset://models/tree.gltf`, or an instance, which stands for every asset that it and its descendants use. `callback` runs once for each item as it finishes, with `Enum.AssetFetchStatus.Success` or `Failure`.

Meshes and images are uploaded to the GPU. A `.surface.hlsl` path compiles the surface shader's pipelines, so they are not created during play when the shader first appears. A sound is opened and its length is read. A name with no `://` is a stamp, named as for `Instance.stamp`: its file is read and kept, and every asset it uses is loaded with it.

Preloaded assets are held for the scene in which they were requested and for the next scene, which is what a loading screen needs. After that they are unloaded like anything else a previous scene used, unless a scene still shows them. To hold assets for the whole game, use `Keep`.

### `Release(items: { string | Instance })`

Stops holding every item that was passed to `Keep`. Nothing is unloaded at once: an asset that no scene shows is unloaded the next time the game leaves a scene.
